lessons.title: Handing Over Work and Tracking Requests
lessons.objective: Learners will understand hand over and keep track of from a workplace handover and use them in new contexts.

reading.text: Before the project lead leaves for annual leave, she will hand over the client schedule to her colleague. They will go over the open tasks in a short video call and flag any deadline that may change. The colleague will keep track of new requests in the shared log and follow up with the design team if a file is missing. A clear handover helps everyone know who is responsible while the lead is away.

sentences.text: Before the project lead leaves for annual leave, she will hand over the client schedule to her colleague.
They will go over the open tasks in a short video call and flag any deadline that may change.
The colleague will keep track of new requests in the shared log and follow up with the design team if a file is missing.
A clear handover helps everyone know who is responsible while the lead is away.

targets.meaningEn: to give responsibility for work to another person
targets.meaningVi: bàn giao công việc cho người khác

targets.meaningEn: to monitor and record the progress of something over time

exercises.prompt: In s1, what does hand over mean when the lead will hand over the client schedule to her colleague?

options.text: It means she will keep the schedule herself and work during her leave.
options.explanation: Wrong because keeping the work contradicts giving responsibility to her colleague.

options.text: It means she will give responsibility for the schedule to her colleague.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches giving work responsibility to another person in this context.

options.text: It means she will postpone the schedule until she returns from leave.
options.explanation: Wrong because postponing delays work rather than transferring responsibility.

exercises.explanation: Hand over here means transferring responsibility for the schedule to the colleague.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that follows the reading's pattern, with 'hand over' immediately before the thing being transferred.

options.text: She will hand over the client schedule to her colleague before she leaves.
options.explanation: Correct because hand over correctly takes the object and to for the receiver.

options.text: She will hand the client schedule over to her colleague before she leaves.
options.explanation: This is grammatical English, but it places the object between hand and over rather than following the pattern requested.

options.text: She will hands over the client schedule to her colleague before she leaves.
options.explanation: Wrong because hands should be hand after the modal will.

exercises.explanation: Only a follows the requested pattern, with hand over immediately before the object; b is a valid alternative word order.

exercises.prompt: In s3, what does keep track of mean when the colleague will keep track of new requests in the shared log?

options.text: It means they will monitor and record new requests over time.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches monitoring and recording progress over time in this context.

options.text: It means they will complete all requests immediately without recording them.
options.explanation: Wrong because completing immediately without recording omits monitoring over time.

options.text: It means they will ignore new requests until someone complains.
options.explanation: Wrong because ignoring requests is the opposite of monitoring and recording them.

exercises.explanation: Keep track of here means monitoring and recording new requests over time.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural correct sentence using keep track of.

options.text: The colleague keeps track on new requests in the shared log every day.
options.explanation: Wrong because the standard phrase is keep track of, not keep track on.

options.text: The colleague keeps track of new requests in the shared log every day.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the standard phrase keep track of with correct grammar.

options.text: The colleague keep track of new requests in the shared log every day.
options.explanation: Wrong because the singular subject the colleague requires keeps, not keep.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses the standard phrase keep track of with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: Imagine you are the captain of a school football team who is graduating. Write 2-3 sentences to the next captain about what duties you will pass to them. Use hand over in your answer.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I will hand over the team equipment and training schedule to you next week. We will meet briefly so you know who to contact for each task.
selfCheck: I used hand over to describe giving responsibility.
I described a school team context, not annual leave.
